summary:
The Confirmation Of Congressional Observer Access Act of 2024 (COCOA Act of 2024) amends the Help America Vote Act of 2002 to require States to provide designated congressional election observers with access to election administration procedures in federal elections.

Section 2 amends Title III of the Help America Vote Act (52 U.S.C. 21081 et seq.) by redesignating sections 304 and 305 as sections 305 and 306, and inserting a new section 304 (52 U.S.C. 21083a note). New section 304 includes a finding of constitutional authority under Article I, Section 5, Clause 1 and Article I, Section 4, Clause 1, clarifying that the section does not establish new authorities but provides a statutory reference for existing congressional authority.

Under new section 304(b), States are required to provide designated congressional election observers full access to clearly observe all elements of election administration procedures, including areas where ballots are cast, processed, scanned, tabulated, canvassed, recounted, audited, or certified, during pre- and post-election procedures. Observers are prohibited from handling ballots or equipment, advocating for positions or candidates, compromising ballot secrecy or voter privacy, or interfering with voters or election administrators. A rule of construction permits observers to ask questions of election officials.

Section 304(c) authorizes State or local election officials to remove an observer if there is a reasonable basis to believe the observer has engaged or will imminently engage in intimidation, deceptive practices prohibited by federal law, or disruption of election processes. Upon removal, the official must notify the chair and ranking minority member of the Committee on House Administration or the Committee on Rules and Administration within 24 hours and provide written notice detailing the reasons. Mere presence is insufficient grounds for removal. The applicable committee chair or ranking minority member may send a replacement observer.

Section 304(d) defines a "designated congressional election observer" as a House or Senate employee designated in writing by the chair or ranking minority member of the relevant committee. Section 304(e) defines "State" to include the 50 states, the District of Columbia, and the U.S. territories.

Section 2(b) makes a conforming amendment to section 401 of the Help America Vote Act (52 U.S.C. 21111) to include section 304 in the Act's enforcement provisions. Section 2(c) updates the table of contents. The Act was approved on October 4, 2024.
